clue.text: Filling, hence making one satisfied

explanation.surface: A sandwich filling that leaves the eater pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Contents are what fills something, and a person who is satisfied is happy with their lot.

clue.text: Half-opening fly, to begin with, is far from gentlemanly

indicators.note: the fly comes at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: the caddis fly is an insect used by anglers

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word half is taken

explanation.surface: A partly open trouser zip is ungentlemanly from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' suggests a trouser zip but is the insect; 'opening' takes H from 'Half', and 'to begin with' puts the fly first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, so caddish conduct is ungallant.

clue.text: Possible outcome of main proposal?

parts.note: main is the sea, and the engagement that follows a proposal becomes a battle at sea

explanation.surface: What a marriage proposal might lead to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the sea; a proposal of marriage leads to an engagement, here a fight between fleets.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle between warships is fought on the open sea.

clue.text: Fish mostly smooth when viewed from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom upwards turns the letters round
mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: A fish that looks mostly smooth from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SLEEK to SLEE, and 'when viewed from below' turns it into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snakelike fish.

clue.text: Local that's of some interest, now?

explanation.surface: A pub that is currently interesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' suggests a pub; in medicine a cream applied to one spot is called topical.
explanation.definitionFit: A topical treatment acts on a particular area of the body, and a topical subject is relevant to current affairs.

clue.text: Two officers holding back one carnivore

indicators.note: the lieutenant's letters hold the next piece between them

parts.note: PO is a petty officer and LT a lieutenant, side by side

indicators.note: back tells us the word for one is read from right to left

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A pair of officers restraining a dangerous meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the card word for one, and 'holding' puts that inside the pair of officers' abbreviations, between the L and the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a small flesh-eating mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Old northerner gives shelter to communist divine

indicators.note: the outer piece takes in and covers the communist

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: An ancient Scot hiding a Marxist cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like a noun for a clergyman; it is the verb, to foresee.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foretell or foresee what will happen.

clue.text: Clergy must not start to appear reluctant

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped from the word for clergy

parts.note: the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Churchmen must not begin to look unwilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To be loth is to be unwilling to do something.

clue.text: Two or three eminent figures in the church?

explanation.surface: A couple of senior churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinals are senior Roman Catholic clergy, so a group of them is literally a set of numbers of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting words such as two and three are the counting set in arithmetic, and the princes of the Catholic church are its cardinals.

clue.text: Misrepresent Italian leader's support for upturn in creativity

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the one above it
in a down entry an upturn reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: art is creative work
Il Duce was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Slander the Italian dictator for backing a creative revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturn in' turns ART into TRA; 'support for' puts DUCE beneath it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to slander or speak falsely of them.

clue.text: Where darkroom technicians work?

parts.note: photographers develop film in a darkroom, so their workplace is the place of developing; the phrase also means a region singled out for economic aid

explanation.surface: A question about the workplace of photographic processors.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a region given government help to attract industry is so called, and film is developed in a darkroom.

clue.text: Man perhaps seen in passage concealing article

indicators.note: the article is tucked away and so drops out of the passage

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between seats
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A man spotted in a corridor hiding some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Bitter creditor obtaining outside help

indicators.note: the creditor's abbreviation gets the help wrapped round it

parts.note: aid means help
CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor

explanation.surface: A resentful lender getting assistance from elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid taste or remark is sharp and harsh, as a bitter one is.

clue.text: Student, one with English university place

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's plate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A student from England securing a university place.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used in 'in lieu of', meaning in place of.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu is an old word for stead or position, as in 'in lieu'.

clue.text: A measure currently in existence

parts.note: a foot is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A unit of length that exists today.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going on or in progress at present is said to be underway in this sense.

clue.text: Senseless, that is — consuming bread

indicators.note: the outer letters eat up the bread

parts.note: IE abbreviates id est, that is
naan is Indian flatbread, also spelt nan

explanation.surface: A remark about pointlessly eating bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane remarks are silly and lacking meaning.

clue.text: Problem few can provide an answer to?

explanation.surface: A riddle that only a small number of people can solve.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult child is a real trial, and a small number of things is only as many as one hand can hold.

clue.text: Vessels seen in a winter resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, to sort the letters again

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ships spotted at a ski holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is the signal to sort the letters of A WINTER again.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots and pans made of tin-plated metal are household vessels.

clue.text: Hamlet possibly with cricket side in deciding match

parts.note: Hamlet is an example of a play by Shakespeare
the off side is half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince joining a cricket team for a final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests a village; it is the play. In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A play-off is an extra game held to settle a tie.

clue.text: Rosemary typically is second, having occupied lead briefly

indicators.note: the second piece has moved into the space inside the lead symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
other means second, as in every other day

explanation.surface: A woman named Rosemary comes second after taking the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosemary' looks like a woman's name but is the kitchen herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a herb grown for cooking, an example of a culinary plant.

clue.text: Road in which there's small hold-up, with wear on periphery

indicators.note: the word for wear sits round the outside of the rest

parts.note: fray means wear away at the edges

indicators.note: in a down entry holding up lifts the word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A highway with a minor traffic jam and worn edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' suggests a traffic jam; in a down entry it means the Scots word for small reads upwards, and 'on periphery' wraps the word for wear round it.
explanation.definitionFit: In America a freeway is a major highway.

clue.text: Substitution you need of noun you mentioned originally?

definitions.text: Substitution you need of noun you mentioned originally?

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the seven words before it

explanation.surface: A question about replacing a noun you used with another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping in a different word of the same meaning for one already used is exactly what this kind of word allows.

clue.text: What infant will do on board -scribbles

indicators.note: on board here means put inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the ship one is on board
a baby crawls before it walks

explanation.surface: A toddler doodling on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is crossword shorthand for aboard ship: the ship's abbreviation goes round the baby's action.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy hasty handwriting is a scrawl.

clue.text: Capital-and I'm so excited for you

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled for a friend in a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the state capital of Wisconsin in the USA.

clue.text: Facilities for drivers by the river

explanation.surface: Golf amenities near a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: The drivers are golf clubs, not motorists; the river runs through north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers place the ball on little pegs before striking with a driver, and the Tees is a river in north-east England.

clue.text: Zoological ancestor of the pelican?

parts.note: reads like animal evolution but means road crossings: the striped crossing came before the light-controlled kind

explanation.surface: An evolutionary question about a sea bird's forebear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pedestrian crossings are named after animals: the striped zebra crossing preceded the push-button pelican crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white striped crossing was introduced in Britain before the signal-controlled one.

clue.text: Amongst which you'll find a group of sulphonamides

indicators.note: a group of letters is taken from inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about a family of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean surrounded by or in the middle of.

clue.text: Wild, bare hillside in the Grampians

indicators.note: wild letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exposed Scottish slope.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grampians are Scottish mountains; brae is the Scots word for a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a steep slope, used across the Scottish highlands.

clue.text: Share out food when told

indicators.note: told means spoken, so we go by how the word sounds

parts.note: meat is food

explanation.surface: Divide up the food when you are instructed to.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to dole or allot portions.

clue.text: Drawing instruments used to improve the design of arches?

definitions.text: Drawing instruments used to improve the design of arches?

parts.words: Drawing instruments used to improve the design of arches?
parts.note: drawing means pulling out hairs, and the arches are those above the eyes

explanation.surface: An architect's tools for sketching better arches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing instruments' suggests pencils and compasses; here they pull out hairs to shape the brows.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pincers pluck stray hairs to shape the arcs above the eyes.

clue.text: Fatty's to be found in the college bar

explanation.surface: An overweight person found in a student bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A buttery is a room in older British colleges where food and drink are served.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rich with fat tastes greasy, and in Oxford and Cambridge colleges a provisions room selling food and drink has this name.

clue.text: New family member walks forward

parts.note: steps means walks
on means forward, as in 'move on'

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the family taking his first steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner's boy from an earlier relationship becomes a recent addition to the household on remarriage.
